deviations: yh_data.csv (2 GB) read with data.table::fread(select=) restricted to the 20 needed columns, to fit the sandbox 4 GB memory / 300 s limits.

Hiring regressions (Tables 1-2) estimated by WLS on cell means (state x month-year x demographic cell x PE group x t-1 status, weighted by summed person weights); point estimates are identical to person-level WLS because every regressor is constant within cells, but clustered SEs are not identical to the person-level ones.

Sample restricted to age < 80 at t-1 (CPS age topcode); this restriction is not stated in the paper but reproduces N = 16,948,516 and the Table 2 subsample Ns exactly. The provided state-unemployment file and state identifiers end in May 2014, so the effective sample ends then.

Wage sample: hires in t with weekly earnings > 0 and allocation flag PRWERNAL == 0 (1994-early 1995 have no flag and drop out); occupation/industry crosswalk code year assigned by date (occ: 1990 codes through 2002, 2002 codes 2003-2010, 2010 codes 2011+; ind: 1990 through 2002, 2002 codes 2003-2008, 2007 codes 2009-2013, 2012 codes 2014+). N = 120,294 vs 112,858 in the paper.
notes: Two exploratory runs (no RESULT lines) checked coding and counts. They showed that the file holds matched t-1/t pairs, and that age<80 reproduces the paper's N exactly. The single scored run (final) estimates all 13 quantities: the hire indicator (x100) covers non-employment->employment, or employed in both months with a changed employer (PUIODP1==2), with self-employment (COW 6,7) not counted; weights are the average of the two months' weights; the state unemployment rate is for month t; demographic FE are sex x white x Hispanic x 7 education groups; SEs are clustered by state. Claimed values were visible in the task, but no comparison-driven change was made after the scored run, so there are no claim attempts. Gaps that remain: experienced preferred 0.055 vs 0.0496, aggregate with month-year FE -0.0286 vs -0.0326, wage N larger than the paper's.
